references.text: Moses fasted for forty days and forty nights on Mount Sinai, parallel to Jesus' forty-day fast.
The forty days of testing for the children of Israel in the wilderness, which mirror Jesus' testing.
Moses' second forty-day fast on Mount Sinai, which also mirrors Jesus' forty-day fast.
God's promise to command His angels to protect, something the devil refers to during the temptation of Jesus.
The prophecy of one crying out in the wilderness, like John the Baptist, who prepares the way for Jesus, who is later tempted in the wilderness.
Matthew's account of Jesus' temptation, which provides a parallel narrative to Luke.
Mark's shorter account of Jesus' temptation in the wilderness.
